A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

lattice QCD calculations can be used to predict hadronic observables with a high degree of accuracy and model-independence, provided that the lattice QCD calculations are carried out with sufficiently small pion mass and sufficiently large volume.
chiral effective field theories formulated with a finite range regulator provide a model-independent extrapolation of lattice results to the physical point.
the quark mass dependence of hadronic properties can be described in terms of a few universal functions, which are determined from a finite number of chiral effective field-theory calculations.

the chiral extrapolation is well under control and that the quark-masses are sufficiently light that chiral non-analities are not suppressed in the physical world.
